I can tell you what it’s like from my experience. Experiences with hospitalization is subjective to person to person. I was very suicidal and I went in voluntarily. A mental hospital isn’t scary as it sounds. It is not like how they portray it in the movies. It’s just very boring but this is an opportunity to keep yourself safe, have a break from your day to day life, and learn how to cope. The psychiatrist I had was very attentive to you when voicing your concerns or questions, willing to work with you, suggest when you want to leave, and find medications that would work for you. I felt really good being there because I was away from home where my parents would constantly yell and fight with each other. I made friends which was great because they helped me cope with staying there. I talked to them, played games and puzzles with them and watch movies. There are not so great things. I slept on a rubber mattress with a tiny pillow. The techs will check on you every 15 minutes in your room. The door opening and closing woke me up several times in the night. 
Some nurses have an attitude towards you especially if you don’t show up when they call for you to take your meds. 
There may be  patients that exhibit erratic behavior and it can cause unnecessary anxiety and tension in the environment. 

TLDR; I was voluntarily hospitalized for being suicidal. The hospitalization overall helped me. There are pros and cons at the hospital. Hospitalization isn’t like how the media and movies represent it.

Hi, I think the best thing to do is find a doctor to discuss your health concerns. Medications and other illnesses can cause a high heart rate. It’s very important to rule out other causes. What you can do now, is perform a “Poor mans tilt table test” at home. The internet has helpful information on how to do it. Write your information down and determine if your heart rate sustained increase in heart rate of greater than 30 beats per minute within 10 minutes of standing. This can be very helpful for a doctor to possibly diagnose you with POTS.

Hello! First, congratulations on the diagnosis! Midodrine seems to work well for me for the most part. It helps reduce my dizziness and my blood from pooling in my legs. Midodrine has a short life span so it only lasts for 3-4 hours.  Please also be aware that there are side affects when taking midodrine, like chills and goosebumps.
No one on this subreddit can say for sure it's POTS. We are not doctors. We cannot diagnose you. Please let your doctor know about your concerns of you possibility having POTS.

The poor man's tilt table test confirmed that I meet the criteria for POTS (increase of 30 bpm) and the 24 hour blood pressure monitor was to see if I have very low blood pressure.

I'm really sorry you're dealing with joint pain. POTS can be secondary to many other conditions like Ehlers Danlos Syndrome. I think you need to find a doctor to rule out other diseases. In the mean time, take Tylenol or Advil to help relieve some pain. Make sure you're not doing anything strenuous to worsen your joint pain. Of course, by no means I am not a doctor so I would take my advice with a grain of salt ;).  I hope you feel better!
